questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I applied for exchange in the final run with very short notice, I had less optional destinations to choose from. From the ones available I prioritized the aspects of transport possibilites (train/bus/public transport connection possibilities) and thoughts about whether I would have opportunities in the future to choose this excactly destination as a place to live for a longer period of time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I find the approach to the teaching in classes very different from what I have been used to, which has been interesting and inspiring, and has as well increased my rate of the overall study abroad experience, which I also found of a lower academic level than what I have been used to at my home university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult to feel sure and safe about the information, that I found on the different webpages and systems, which made it crucial to me that I was able to email and communicate with administratives at both my home and host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I mainly received assistance to student and document registration. I also attended an online introduction meeting, which was useful to sum um basic deadlines and places to take notice of.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I found that the availability to communicate with administratives and receive help and answers to questions was very accessible, but that I wouldn't have managed only through the online orientation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was a part of a three-person group and not in charge of finding the housing. I don't think it was too difficult to find the housing through online groups and seraches, but that it of course takes some time and orientation to make sure that the pricing is reasonable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in an accomodation off campus housing, where many other erasmus exchange students also lived. This I found very valuable, because the social sorroundings and network established a common neighbourhood feeling

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think of the process as partly managable in an intuitive way, but also with many different sorts of websides, deadlines and info to have a hold on. to me it was very helpfull to create and continuously update a document with every single step/change/accomplishment in the proces, to even a have a sort of hold of the whole. This made it less stressful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration had multiple steps, which first had to settle the acceptance as a student of the host university, and from then on registrations on the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was informed, that I could contact the administration of my home university and of my host university. And besides of course search for help through the webpages

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up with the classes, that I wanted to register for, but I found it difficult to get an overview of the actual courses available until the very day of registration. The system in which the courses are registrered and appear is difficult to search within.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend to look up kinds of classes, that has an interest, but to not settle for final choices until just before the atual day of registration, as the classes may not be available at the term. I would also recommend to have gathered a list of more classes than actually needed, in case you don't get a spot in the class, as well as to be ready to apply the minute the registration day opens up, because some classes may be filled up in very short time.
I also recommend to attend more classes than needed during the first few weeks, as the period of registration is interchangable within the first few weeks of the term. This I found very nice - that I was able to attend classes and cancel them afterwards, if I was not interested anyway.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many very interesting classes where available. It was admirable to experience that the classes set up even if the amount of students for the class is little.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level or the formalities and requirements less academicly strict, which overall gave an impression of a lower academic level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was more in touch with the students in a way of including or depending on their presence.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Czech Modern & Contemporary Art & Architecture.
Game Theory.
Politics, Culture & Visuality: Czech and Slovak Film 1950 - 2000.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I found all three courses very inspiring and educational from my points of interests. At the same time, specifically the czech film course and the czech art & architecture class, both had a broad focus on czech history, which I appreciated alot.

I also very much recommend to attend the pre-term introduction language course, if it is available! It was a key decision for my stay an introduction to people, the culture and the city in overall.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I encountered unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transport was very cheap and cheaper than expected. The generel living expenses are very cheap compared to danish costs.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I personally did not attend many non-academic opportunities, but I have the impression that the oportunities were many and varying.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have heard of different sports activities such as hikes and ball-sports. Many tours round the city were arranged by the esn association, as well as pubcrawl, quizzes etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend attending the social activites arranged, if they are of interest, as it is a fine opportunity to meet other excange student at an early point. I would though also not feel pressure to attend, if not feeling like it at first. There are plenty of opportunities to meet people during the stay.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: personally I have prioritized to spend ad much time in the city, which I exchanged to, and the outskirts of it, as I wanted to realy get to know the town that I was living in. I also enjoyed a few travels out of town, but mainyl stayed in the town and used alld ifferent sites, and cultural facilities that was always tending new events in th weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easier than expected, as I found some suprising similarities to danish culture and behavoral aspects. at the same time I found it of great help to have attended the pre-term intensive language course - a key element to adjust to the local culture for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think a difference not big but present would be regarding behaviour in public space and a certain sense of a specific politeness or rudeness, which I take notice of to be able to adjust to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Overall I found the atmosphere of the city safe and relaxed. Of cultural experiences I appreciated the film and arts alot, there are many incredible museums and kinos to attend and visit!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
In the proces of registration I found it usefull to keep a 'diary' with all changes/deadlines/accomplishments, to keep an overall overview of te process.
In the proces choosing courses I recommend to register for and attend more courses than needed, and then to unregister from some of them again - to take use of the possibility to try courses before settling for good.
I also recommend to live central enough to be able to travel by feet at least to some extend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The workload varies alot from course to course. Maybe that is a good thing to ave in mind when putting together a scheme of courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: As this was my first experience of staying abroad for a longer period of time, to me this part is definitely the most rewarding of my exchange experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: On a practical level I think it was a challenge to settled on my final scheme as the registration system and procedure was entagling and long.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I deeply recommend attending the pre-term language course, if it is offered.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
